patch_description: Instead of ranking k candidate paths once and round-robining partitions, this approach treats broadcast routing as an iterative congestion-aware assignment problem. It generates a large pool of candidate paths per destination using cost-weighted randomized edge sampling (a Monte-Carlo / ant-colony style exploration around the cheapest routes), then assigns each partition greedily by marginal cost: path_cost + λ·(current_edge_load / throughput). This lets cheap shared trunk edges absorb most partitions while lightly penalizing congestion, and expensive detours only get used when the cheap route is saturated. Load and cost are jointly optimized instead of being sequentially ranked, which should lower combined cost while keeping transfers overlappable across parallel links.
